title: Fynaptix · AI & Compute Research
heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI is the market's most crowded trade; concentration and drawdown risk are significant. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Amazon (raised again to ~$220B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (~$175B CY2026 guide / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($135–145B) and Oracle (S&P now models $90–95B FY2027, up from the company's earlier ~$70B target) — combined $815–840B, still ~75% AI-specific and now well over 3x the ~$238B spent in 2024. Debt funding sits at 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet); Oracle says it won't add more debt in CY2026, leaning instead on a $20B at-the-market equity raise after its Aug 25 downgrade to BBB-

Revenue run-rate held near $65B annualized at end of July with the company's first-ever operating profit. Reports now point to an Oct 26 IPO with a first-day market cap near $1.82T, and some accounts still float $2T or more — which would eclipse SpaceX's $1.77T IPO valuation as the largest listing ever

Global venture funding per Crunchbase ($300B in Q1, $205B in Q2), already topping all of 2025's $440B; AI captured ~70–80% of it. OpenAI and Anthropic alone absorbed $217B — 43% of every venture dollar invested worldwide this year

kpis.sub: NVIDIA Q2 FY27 REVENUE — RECORD (REPORTED AUG 26)
kpis.label: Revenue more than doubled YoY (+106%), beating the ~$92.2B consensus; Data Center revenue hit $89.0B (+117% YoY). Guided Q3 to $108B. Shares dipped slightly in the immediate reaction before the broader market rallied the next session (Nasdaq +1.6%) — the clearest data point yet against the bubble case, even as Nvidia also disclosed talks to buy Hugging Face for $12.9B and keeps defending its OpenAI financing structure against circular-financing criticism

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: Sequoia's own framework for the revenue needed to justify AI capex has risen from $200B (late 2023) to roughly $600B today; actual AI-attributable revenue is estimated at just $50–150B annually (Exponential View pegs the broader generative-AI run rate near $175B) — a 4–13x gap that keeps widening as the top-5 hyperscaler 2026/FY27 capex total climbs to $815–840B. The BIS's June 2026 annual report names an AI-capex bust as one of its top three risks to global financial stability.

bear_case.title: Rates are the transmission mechanism — but strength can still win the argument
bear_case.description: The Aug 18 rate-driven selloff (30-year Treasury at 5.32%, SOXX -4.96%, CoreWeave -12%) argued a debt-funded buildout is now exposed to financing-cost risk, not just AI-demand risk. But NVIDIA's Aug 26 beat-and-raise ($96.2B revenue, $108B Q3 guide) helped the Nasdaq rally 1.6% the next session, and commentary has already started citing names like Microsoft, TSMC and Cisco as evidence the bubble narrative is losing its best argument — a reminder the debate can swing hard in either direction week to week.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments sitting off hyperscaler balance sheets, with debt funding of the buildout holding near 32% of capex over the trailing twelve months (FactSet). Oracle is now the starkest case: S&P downgraded its credit to BBB- on Aug 25 (one notch above junk), FY26 free cash flow already came in at -$23.7B, and S&P projects the deficit widening to ~$42B in FY27 even as the company insists it won't add more debt this calendar year — leaning on a $20B equity raise instead.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: Nvidia's proposed OpenAI financing backstop was cut from an originally floated $250B to under $120B and now covers only the first phase of an Ohio data center — a sign the market's pushback on "vendor financing its own customers" is affecting deal structure. Jensen Huang insists the arrangement isn't circular financing, but Michael Burry has escalated, calling Nvidia's revenue "majority circularly financed" and adding shorts on Oracle, Micron and Nebius plus March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF. Nvidia's own reported $12.9B pursuit of Hugging Face (Aug 26) extends the web one layer further, from chips into the model-hosting layer its customers depend on.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; bears argue the real economic life is closer to 2–3 years, understating depreciation by an estimated ~$176B across 2026–2028 and flattering reported earnings (Oracle by an estimated 26.9%, Meta by 20.8%, by 2028 on this analysis). Michael Burry has doubled down on shorts in Oracle, Micron and Nebius, plus fresh March 2027 puts on the semiconductor ETF, calling current pricing "what the top of a boom looks like." Counterpoint: NVIDIA and CoreWeave point to secondary-market pricing and long-term contracts as evidence older silicon stays productive longer than the bear case assumes.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Oracle is planning another round of job cuts ahead of the Sept 1 start of its fiscal Q2 — on top of the ~21,000 already cut — even as S&P now models $90–95B of FY2027 capex funded substantially by a fresh equity raise. Microsoft cut roughly 4,800 more in July. Tech-sector layoffs remain near a 20-year high. The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, shrinking headcount, and disclosures like Meta's own AI systems breaching internal test environments — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean on cost-cutting elsewhere in the business, not on AI revenue itself.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once, as the Aug 18 rate-driven selloff already demonstrated across chip names. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters (NVIDIA's actual $96.2B Q2 FY27 print, TSMC's 2nm ramp running ahead of schedule) — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals.

catalysts.title: Nvidia reportedly agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.9B
catalysts.description: The unconfirmed deal would extend Nvidia's reach from chips into the open-source model-hosting layer millions of developers use daily.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Actual Q2 FY27 print beat and raised — $96.2B revenue (+106% YoY), Data Center $89.0B (+117%), $108B Q3 guide — real external revenue growth that's hard to dismiss even as Michael Burry escalates his "majority circularly financed" charge and the OpenAI financing guarantee gets scaled back. Also sits in this hub's Quantum, Robotics and AI Biotech sleeves — don't double-count sizing.

positions.name: TSMC
positions.note: 2nm ramp is running ahead of schedule — monthly wafer starts tracking toward ~100K by year-end with tape-outs already 4x 3nm's pace at the same stage — extending the runway with the least circular-financing exposure of any name on this page. Taiwan geopolitical risk remains the single largest tail risk in the entire hub.

positions.name: Alphabet
positions.note: Still the only genuinely full-stack position — TPUs, Gemini, Waymo (now expanding robotaxis across all of coastal California). Capex guide has held steady at $195–205B for two straight editions rather than escalating further, a rare sign of discipline in this group. Also appears in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Azure's $80B unfulfilled order backlog (power-constrained, not demand-constrained) remains the standout bull signal, unchanged this week. FY2027 all-in spend is still estimated near $255–260B once leased capacity is counted. Also in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Amazon
positions.note: Capex guide raised again this week to ~$220B (from ~$200B) with no sign the market minds — AWS's 37% growth (fastest in 18 quarters) keeps giving Amazon the clearest capex-payback story of the group. Sizing up to reflect that combination of raised spend and unbroken investor confidence.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: AI bookings/backlog above $30B and shares rallied 4.5% into the Sept 2 print, but last quarter's failure to raise the FY2027 AI-semi target above $100B triggered a 12.6% selloff — an unresolved question that makes this week's earnings a real test rather than a formality.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Moving off Core this week: shares are up over 40% in a single month on top of an already-stretched multiple, and while the Army contract win is real, a lost French DGSI contract shows the growth story isn't purely one-directional. Good business — the price now assumes flawless execution indefinitely, which is a Watch, not a Core, situation.

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: Strong Q2 print (EPS $1.66 vs $0.48 a year ago) but the stock slipped on its own ROCm 10 launch and Cathie Wood reportedly trimmed her stake the same day — the kind of whipsaw that belongs in speculative sizing, not core.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: CFO Susan Li's "highly dynamic" 2026 capital planning still means no fixed capex ceiling, and the CoreWeave capacity expansion to $21B adds more off-books-style spend on top of an already capex-skeptical market reaction — no new evidence this week to move off Watch.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.note: The Aug 25 downgrade to BBB- (one notch above junk), a widening FY27 free-cash-flow deficit projected near $42B, and yet another round of layoffs planned before Sept 1 all confirm rather than change last week's Avoid — the backlog story keeps getting more expensive to sustain.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: Nothing this week changes the core problem: being disrupted by the agent wave it markets itself as part of.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: Grok 4.6's launch keeps xAI competitive on capability, but the capex burn (Q2 more than doubled to $15.8B) still outruns confirmed new revenue like the Alphabet GPU deal. Not enough clarity yet to move off Watch.
